title: Russian Overnight Barrage Damages 21-Story Odesa Apartment Building, Injuring 17
detail: Russia launched a large overnight aerial assault on Ukraine involving 174 attack drones, two ballistic missiles, and two air-launched missiles, with Odesa among the hardest-hit cities. A strike damaged 20 apartments between the 10th and 17th floors of a 21-story residential building and destroyed 12 parked cars nearby, injuring 17 people including 3 children. Odesa City Military Administration head Serhii Lysak said eight of the injured came from the residential building itself, with additional casualties from strikes on other infrastructure across the city. Russia's Defense Ministry claimed it targeted port and military-related infrastructure; Ukrainian officials said residential areas were hit.

title: Ukrainian Strike on Shebekino, Belgorod Region, Kills 4 Including Two Medical Personnel
detail: A Ukrainian strike on Shebekino, a Russian border town in Belgorod Region roughly 5 km from Ukraine, killed 4 people on September 3 — a doctor, a medic, and a married couple — and injured 3 others, according to acting regional governor Alexander Shuvayev. Several houses and vehicles were damaged. The strike was part of a broader wave of roughly 180 Ukrainian attacks on Belgorod Region over the prior 24 hours, which separately killed 1 civilian and injured 21 (including 2 children) region-wide. Separately, the head of Russian-controlled Donetsk Region said Ukrainian drone strikes killed 3 civilians across three districts the same day.

title: Putin Says There Is a 'Chance' of a Peace Deal as Ukraine Sees a 'New Dynamic' in Talks
detail: Speaking at an economic forum in Russia's far east on September 3, President Putin said there was a chance of reaching an agreement to end the war, adding that the US and China were among countries ready to support a settlement, though he said it was difficult to assess how far ongoing contacts — mostly 'through intelligence channels' — were advancing peace. Putin also said Ukrainian drone strikes on civilian vessels amounted to 'acts of state terrorism' that complicate talks. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said he expects a 'new dynamic' in peace efforts, with renewed diplomatic engagement across capitals, and President Zelensky said US negotiators would soon visit both Moscow and Kyiv.

title: Ukrainian Naval Drone Strikes Russian Vessel in Sochi Port — First-Ever USV Attack on Putin's Resort City
detail: Ukraine's Naval Forces struck the Nefrit, a Russian-flagged multipurpose support vessel, with an unmanned surface vessel (USV) in the port of Sochi on September 3 — the first known Ukrainian USV attack on the Black Sea resort city Putin frequently visits, roughly 650-700 km from the Ukrainian border. The Nefrit supported Russia's offshore oil and gas operations, cargo and personnel transport, and underwater technical work; Ukrainian officials said the strike targeted 'the enemy's logistics, specialized capabilities and military-economic infrastructure.' Footage circulating on Russian Telegram channels into September 4 also showed a fire at an oil depot near the port and reports of an explosion near a Pantsir air defense system, though Kyiv Independent said it could not independently verify the extent of the damage.
